report.summary: The bug was in `load()` in `public/src/store.js`. Its error handler set `orders: []`, so any failed load wiped the list. A failed refresh therefore left only the error message. I removed that line, so a failed load now leaves the orders alone and only sets `loading: false` and the error. The message is still "Could not refresh orders." once the first load has succeeded, and "Could not load orders." before that. A successful load still sets `error: null`, so the message goes away on the next good refresh (ORD-3). Switching to a different filter still clears the old rows first, so the old filter's rows never show under the new one (ORD-2). I added a regression test to `test/store.test.js` for a failed refresh keeping the orders and the next good refresh clearing the message.
report.verification: `npm test` passes, 5 of 5, including the new test. I also ran the registry check `orders-refresh-keeps-orders` (observe with `checks/refresh-steps.json`) in a real browser against the fixed app. It injected one HTTP 503 on the refresh read, and both `orders-kept` and `refresh-error-shown` completed, with 8 order rows still on screen after the failed refresh. I did not record a before-change baseline or run `compare_reports`, because I edited the code before running any check. So there is no before/after comparison, only this run on the fixed code. The check covers one 503 on a refresh of the All list, not other filters, offline mode or first loads. I stopped the server and browser launcher I started, and nothing is still listening on ports 4173 or 9222.
